subject: Business Models
title: The Factory System
description: A 60-second lesson on The Factory System.

hook.text: Before factories, goods were made at home by hand. One weaver produced a few yards of cloth per day.

buildup.text: Richard Arkwright's cotton mills in the 1770s gathered workers, machines, and power in one building.

discovery.text: Factories divided labor into simple, repetitive tasks. Output per worker multiplied tenfold.

twist.text: Workers hated it. The Luddites smashed machines, fearing technology would destroy their livelihoods.

climax.text: Factories won. Mass production made goods affordable for millions who could never buy them before.

punchline.text: Cheap goods, hard labor. Factories changed everything.

quiz.question: Who pioneered the factory system for cotton mills?

details.summary: The factory system replaced cottage industry by concentrating workers, machinery, and raw materials in a single location. Beginning with textile mills in 18th century England, it introduced mechanized production, division of labor, and wage employment.
details.whyItMatters: The factory system created the modern economy. It shifted production from homes to centralized workplaces, creating urbanization, the working class, industrial capitalism.
takeaways: Factories centralized workers and machines for mechanized, large-scale production
Division of labor and specialization dramatically increased output per worker
The factory system drove urbanization and created the modern wage-labor economy

faq.question: What advantages did factories have over cottage industry?
faq.answer: Centralized power sources like water wheels and steam engines drove machinery impossible in homes. Division of labor increased specialization and speed. Quality control was possible with supervised production..

faq.question: What were the social consequences of the factory system?
faq.answer: Mass urbanization as workers moved from farms to factory cities. Child labor exploitation in dangerous conditions. Formation of the working class and labor movements. Destruction of artisan livelihoods..
